question: Which original studies (RCTs and NRSIs) compare larger versus smaller RBC volume per transfusion for anemia in hospitalized adults, children and preterm neonates?

claims.text: Infants with birth weight 500 to 1,500 g were randomly assigned to 10 or 20 mL/kg red blood cells; post-transfusion hemoglobin was 14.2 versus 12.0 g/dL with 20 versus 10 mL/kg.
fragments: Infants with birth weights between 500 and 1,500 g were randomly assigned to receive 10 or 20 mL/kg red blood cells.
Infants with transfusions of 20 mL/kg had a greater hemoglobin (14.2 +/- 1.9 vs. 12.0 +/- 1.9 g/dL

elements.source: randomly assigned to receive 10 or 20 mL/kg

claims.text: Mallett: 22 hemodynamically stable VLBW infants in a randomized crossover study of 20 versus 15 mL/kg; hemoglobin 13.2 versus 11.8 g/dL.
fragments: The study enrolled 22 hemodynamically stable VLBW infants requiring PRBC transfusions
Infants had higher posttransfusion hemoglobin (13.2 g/dL vs 11.8 g/dL, P < 0.01)

claims.text: Chen: 73 newborns received 20 ml/kg and 78 received 15 ml/kg; transfusions 1.9 versus 2.6.
fragments: 73 newborns received 20 ml/kg (large volume group) and 78 newborns received 15 ml/kg transfusion (small volume group).
The transfusion number of the large volume group is significantly less than that of the small volume group (1.9 ± 0.3 vs. 2.6 ± 0.9

elements.source: 73 newborns received 20 ml/kg ... 78 newborns received 15 ml/kg

claims.text: TRACT: 3196 African children with hemoglobin below 6 g/dL randomised to 20 versus 30 mL/kg; 28-day mortality 3.4% versus 4.5% (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.54 to 1.08).
claims.discrepancy: direction/arm assignment: the card lists 20 versus 30 mL/kg with 3.4% versus 4.5%, which gives the 20 mL/kg arm the lower mortality. In the source, 3.4% is the 30 mL/kg arm and 4.5% is the 20 mL/kg arm. The HR of 0.76 also compares 30 with 20 mL/kg.
fragments: 55 children (3.4%) in the higher-volume group and 72 (4.5%) in the lower-volume group died before 28 days (hazard ratio, 0.76; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.54 to 1.08
A total of 3196 eligible children (median age, 37 months; 2050 [64.1%] with malaria) were assigned to receive a transfusion of 30 ml per kilogram (1598 children) or 20 ml per kilogram (1598 children)

elements.source: 3196 children, Hb <6 g/dL, Uganda and Malawi

elements.card: 3.4% versus 4.5%, listed in the order 20 vs 30 mL/kg, so 3.4% for 20 mL/kg
elements.source: 3.4% was in the 30 mL/kg (higher-volume) group and 4.5% in the 20 mL/kg (lower-volume) group
HR 0.76 (0.54 to 1.08), for higher vs lower volume

claims.text: Byun: pilot randomised factorial trial in 91 AML patients on chemotherapy comparing Hb trigger 7 versus 8 g/dL and single versus double unit per transfusion; units per transfusion did not change total RBC use, outcomes or bleeding.
fragments: Initially 91 patients were randomized into 4 groups, but the protocol adherence rate was 90.1%.

The number of RBC units per transfusion did not affect the total 
amount of RBC transfusion required during treatment. AML treatment outcomes and 
bleeding events did not differ across the 4 groups.

elements.card: pilot randomised 2x2 factorial, Hb trigger 7 vs 8 and single vs double unit
elements.source: 2 by 2 factorial design, trigger 7 vs 8 g/dL, single vs double-unit

elements.card: units per transfusion did not change total RBC use, outcomes or bleeding
elements.source: did not affect the total amount of RBC transfusion; outcomes and bleeding did not differ across the 4 groups

claims.text: Marco-Ayala: 187 patients under a single-unit policy versus 153 historical double-unit patients in autologous stem cell transplant; RBC use fell 32%; length of stay, discharge Hb and 30-day mortality did not differ.
fragments:
of 187 patients transplanted from May 2019 to December 2022 under a 1-RBC 
policy, with a historical cohort of 153 patients

The 1-RBC policy was associated with a 
32% reduction in RBC utilization

differences in length of stay, hemoglobin levels at discharge or 30-day 
mortality were observed.

fragments:

fragments:

fragments:

claims.text: Heyes: six months before and after implementation of a single unit policy on eight general medical wards; single-unit orders rose from 30% to 53%.
fragments:
eight general medical wards and all staff working in the blood transfusion 
laboratory. We collected transfusion data for 12 months, (6 months before and 
after implementation).

The number of single unit 
transfusions, increased from 30 to 53% whilst the number of two units decreased 
from 65 to 43% (P < 0.001).
